units.source_text: 母亲很相信当时我说的话。

en.t: Mother truly believed what I had said at the time.

units.source_text: 那时，我向她保证过，先生一定会回信的。

en.t: At that time, I had assured her that Sensei would certainly write back.

units.source_text: 但是，我根本没有指望会收到父母所期望的那样的回信。

en.t: But I had never really expected to receive the kind of reply my parents were hoping for.

units.source_text: 其结果，就像我是故意要欺骗母亲似的。

en.t: As a result, it was as though I had deliberately deceived Mother.
Write another letter to him, Mother said.

units.source_text: 倘若能使母亲感到安慰，写多少封没用的信，我也不嫌麻烦。

en.t: If it would comfort Mother, I did not mind writing any number of useless letters.

units.source_text: 但是一再向先生拜托这种事情，使我感到痛苦，比起挨父亲训斥、惹母亲生气来，我觉得被先生看不起要可怕得多。

en.t: But repeatedly asking Sensei for this sort of thing pained me; I found being looked down on by Sensei far more frightening than being scolded by Father or upsetting Mother.

units.source_text: 我也猜测过，至今没收到先生的回信，莫非就是这个原因？

en.t: I even wondered whether this might be the very reason I had still received no reply from Sensei.

units.source_text: “写封信很简单，可这种事儿，光靠写信是不会有什么结果的。

en.t: Writing a letter is easy, but with this kind of matter, letters alone will not accomplish anything.

units.source_text: 我必须到东京去一趟，直接拜托人家才行。”

en.t: I have to go to Tokyo myself and ask him directly.

units.source_text: “可是你爸病成这样，你还不知什么时候能到东京去呢！”

en.t: But with your father as ill as this, who knows when you will be able to go to Tokyo?
That is why I have not gone.

units.source_text: 我想，在爸的病还没有眉目之前，先不去东京了。”

en.t: I think I will stay away from Tokyo until we know how Father's illness is going to turn out.

units.source_text: 怎么能放着这么重的病人不管，自己去东京呢。”

en.t: How could anyone leave such a seriously ill person unattended and go off to Tokyo on his own?
